See also: Jaz, jaź, jaż, jáz, jaž, and яз

Translingual

[edit]

Symbol

[edit]

jaz

  1. (international standards) ISO 639-3 language code for Jawe.

See also

[edit]
  • Wiktionary’s coverage of Jawe terms

English

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

jaz (uncountable)

  1. Dated spelling of jazz (“musical style”).

Old Slovak

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ězъ.

Noun

[edit]

jaz m inan

  1. weir

Further reading

[edit]
  • Majtán, Milan et al., editors (1991–2008), “jaz”, in Historický slovník slovenského jazyka [Historical Dictionary of the Slovak Language] (in Slovak), volumes 1–7 (A – Ž), Bratislava: VEDA, →OCLC

Polish

[edit]
Polish Wikipedia has an article on:
jaz
Wikipedia pl

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • IPA(key): /ˈjas/
  • (Masovia):
    • (Far Masovian) IPA(key): [ˈjas]
    • (Łowicz) IPA(key): [ˈjas]
  • (Lesser Poland):
    • (Western Kraków) IPA(key): [ˈjas]
    • (Lasovia) IPA(key): [ˈjas]
    • (Podegrodzie) IPA(key): [ˈjas]
    • (Western Lublin) IPA(key): [ˈjas]
    • (Przemyśl) IPA(key): [ˈjas]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -as
  • Syllabification: jaz

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ězъ.

Noun

[edit]

jaz m inan

  1. weir (type of dam)
Declension
[edit]
Declension of jaz
singular plural
nominative jaz jazy
genitive jazu jazów
dative jazowi jazom
accusative jaz jazy
instrumental jazem jazami
locative jazie jazach
vocative jazie jazy

Etymology 2

[edit]

See aż.

Conjunction

[edit]

jaz

  1. (Łowicz, Western Kraków, Pilica, Lasovia, Sandomierz, Zawichost, Góry Wysokie, Stare Kichary, Podegrodzie, Nowy Sącz, Zabrzeż, Zawada, Western Lublin, Ponikwoda, Przemyśl, Rzeszów) alternative form of aż

Particle

[edit]

jaz

  1. (Far Masovian, Przasnysz, Western Kraków, Zebrzydowice, Western Lublin, Ponikwoda, Przemyśl, Rzeszów) alternative form of aż

Further reading

[edit]
  • jaz in Polish dictionaries at PWN

  • Encyklopedia staropolska/Jaz on the Polish Wikisource.Wikisource pl
  • Aleksander Saloni (1908), “jaz”, in “Lud rzeszowski”, in Materyały Antropologiczno-Archeologiczne i Etnograficzne‎[1] (in Polish), volume 10, Kraków: Akademia Umiejętności, page 335
  • Marzena Kozanecka-Zwierz, Magdalena Bartosiewicz, Renata Marciniak-Firadza, editors (2014), “jaz”, in Gwara – Księżaków "język ojczysty" Dziedzictwo regionu łowickiego (in Polish), Łowicz: Muzeum w Łowiczu, →ISBN, page 19

Portuguese

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈʒa(j)s/ [ˈʒa(ɪ̯)s]
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈʒa(j)s/ [ˈʒa(ɪ̯)s]
    • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /ˈʒa(j)ʃ/ [ˈʒa(ɪ̯)ʃ]
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈʒaʃ/

  • Rhymes: (Brazil) -as, (Portugal, Rio de Janeiro) -aʃ, (Brazil) -ajs, (Rio de Janeiro) -ajʃ
  • Hyphenation: jaz

Verb

[edit]

jaz

  1. inflection of jazer:
    1. third-person singular present indicative
    2. second-person singular imperative

Serbo-Croatian

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ězъ.

Noun

[edit]

jȃz m inan (Cyrillic spelling ја̑з)

  1. abyss
  2. (figuratively) gap
Declension
[edit]
Declension of jaz
singular plural
nominative jȃz jȁzovi
genitive jȃza jazóvā
dative jȃzu jazòvima
accusative jȃz jȁzove
vocative jȃze jȁzovi
locative jázu jazòvima
instrumental jȃzom jazòvima

Etymology 2

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *(j)azъ, from Proto-Indo-European *éǵh₂.

Pronoun

[edit]

jaz ? (Cyrillic spelling јаз)

  1. (Chakavian, Kajkavian, regional) I
    Synonym: (Standard) ja

Slovene

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *(j)azъ, from Proto-Indo-European *éǵh₂. First attested in the 10th century.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /jás/

Pronoun

[edit]

jȁz

  1. I
    Synonym: see Thesaurus:jaz
    Jaz sem Slovenec. ― I am a Slovene.

Declension

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

jȁz m inan

  1. (literary) an individual and its personality, ego
